newsitem.title: MOROCCO: France seeks EU equality for Mediterranean and East.
newsitem.headline: France seeks EU equality for Mediterranean and East.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine said on Tuesday that France did not want the European Union to neglect its Mediterranean neighbours in favour of East European countries.
"My first visit was to Morocco because we do not wish to create a gathering which would exclude Mediterranean countries in favour of East Europe and Russia," he told a news conference in Rabat.
Vedrine became foreign minister when the socialist party took power in France last month and was on his first trip to a non-EU country.
Answering a question on the Middle East, he said: "There are unfortunately no European initiatives .... that would mean that we have a way to give a new impulse to the Middle East process.
"But what is happening is that a number of countries notably France are preoccupied with the situation and think they have to find one way or another to relaunch the process.
Turning to relations between Morocco and France, Vedrine said there was no visa problems between the two.
"There is a problem in general connected to France and the countries of the Shengen space (EU countries in agreement to allow those with visas for one territory to cross borders to another).
"It is true that we (France) had reached an exaggeratedly brutal system...(but) the new government has decided to approach the situation with more flexibility."

Speaking of Franco-Moroccan economic relations, the minister said: "If France wants more investments in Morocco (its) investors must present good projects. This does not depend on a political decision."
Vedrine arrived in Morocco on Monday for a two-day visit, during which he had talks with King Hassan and Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali.
Diplomatic sources said earlier that Vedrine was preparing for a visit by French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, expected before the end of this year.
